Subject: DPA annex questions — private deployment key custody and egress

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo today. We’re evaluating Redwood Private for our VPC/on-prem option and legal asked for a short annex to the DPA to capture two things before we proceed: (1) confirmation that customer-managed keys are supported without mandatory provider escrow, and (2) an explicit data egress matrix showing what telemetry or logs (if any) leave our VPC during normal ops and during break-glass operator support.

We have a few constraints: we must retain sole ownership of master keys (HSM-backed is preferred), no provider-side key copies unless explicitly agreed, and cross-border transfers require written approval for EU->US flows.

I attached a draft annex and a quick spreadsheet with our expected flows. Can you confirm whether Redwood can sign something aligned to these points or if you need changes to your operating model?

Best,

Karthik / Priya,

High level summary from the infra side: we can support customer-controlled keys in two practical patterns for Private (VPC/on-prem):

1) Customer-managed KMS (preferred): customer brings HSM-backed KMS in their VPC; Redwood ships a key-wrapping integration (we never store plaintext keys). No escrow required. Operationally we still need a short-lived service account certificate for agent bootstrap; that cert does NOT allow key unwrap.

2) Customer keys + optional host escrow: customer provides keys and a sealed-escrow mechanism can be used only under mutually agreed break-glass (both parties sign a release). This is heavier and we generally avoid it for regulated health customers.

Telemetry / egress we typically see:
- Heartbeat and agent health pings (non-PII metrics) — configurable to be private-only, can be disabled.
- Aggregate usage counters for billing (token counts) — can be computed locally and shared as a signed report on demand.
- Crash dumps / core traces — not collected by default; only if customer enables crash reporting.
- Operator support session recordings (if enabled) — explicit consent + signed request; otherwise sessions are local and ephemeral.

I attached a proposed egress matrix that maps each category to a default behavior and an opt-in/opt-out. Short list of constraints/notes:
- EU->US transfers: we can disable automated telemetry and require an explicit data transfer approval flow (email/DocuSign) for any diagnostic snapshot that crosses borders.
- Break-glass: we can add an annex that requires (a) customer-signed release, (b) limited scope by timestamp/model, and (c) not to be used for historical data retrieval.

Attachment: custkey-egress-matrix.xlsx (I populated the matrix with defaults and opt-outs).

If legal wants fallback language for escrow alternatives, we should propose an SLA credit plus a short canary run for acceptance tests instead of escrow.

-Mina
Engineering Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

All,

This reads reasonable and aligns with our standard DPA annex playbook for regulated customers. A few legal/pricing notes:
- No-escrow is acceptable for enterprise with a governance addendum (we require an Operator Access Addendum and documented break-glass procedure).
- We should include an audit clause: customer can request an operator audit once per year under NDA to confirm no provider key copies exist.
- For billing tokens: offer signed usage attestations monthly instead of continuous counters if they want reduced telemetry.

I'll draft suggested annex language (2–3 paragraphs) and a short checklist for the DocuSign approval flow. If we agree on Mina’s matrix I’ll iterate and share with Miguel.

Thanks — Priya
Chief of Staff, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
